title: Four selection passes, followed by ranking
notes:
SLIDE 4 · 45 seconds · 02:20–03:05 · Miguel
The overview has two stages: selection, then ranking. Triage assesses relevance. IV rescue looks for disability rulings with rules that transfer to accident insurance. ATSG rescue revisits candidates those passes rejected, asking for a quotation from the ruling. Critical review weighs the available evidence against the source text. Earlier positives are preserved and plausible additions become borderline cases. The ranker then combines Apertus assessments using weights learned from Suva's labels. Relevant cases come first, with borderline cases below them.

title: Benchmarking frontier models improved
notes:
SLIDE 5 · 55 seconds · 03:05–04:00 · Miguel
We used independent frontier-model rankings to identify where Apertus needed better prompts. Codex, Gemini, Muse and Claude ranked the same cases blind. We normalised their scores to percentile ranks and combined them using weights calibrated on labelled cases. Comparing that consensus with Apertus exposed general patterns, such as overvaluing an individual remand and undervaluing a rule with broad effect. Those lessons informed more precise system prompts and ranking criteria. The graph shows top-ten overlap in June. The final ranker still uses Apertus's own assessments and case facts, with weights learned from Suva's yes-or-no list. We compare ranking methods through cross-validation. Frontier-model outputs are development references, not runtime inputs.

title: Our summaries retain the key legal points
notes:
SLIDE 6 · 45 seconds · 04:00–04:45 · Miguel
The message is that our summaries retain most of the legal substance in Suva’s expert summaries. Coverage measures retained key legal points, not overall factual accuracy. First, Apertus extracts two to six key legal points from each Suva expert summary. In a separate judging call, it checks our summary against those points. Each point earns one for covered, half for partial and zero for missing. We average within a ruling, then across the held-out rulings. That gives 94.7 percent mean coverage across 19 examples. The expert comparison below shows the same ruling on both sides. We also check outcomes, consideration references and insurer names automatically.
